title: Lossless Address Coding for Quantum Networks
abstract: As quantum systems advance toward interconnected architectures, the ability to identify nodes, manage resources, and support network-level functions becomes increasingly critical. In this work, we propose a lossless source coding scheme for addressing in quantum networks that enables compact, hierarchical, and coherently processable quantum address states. Specifically, we introduce a prefix-suffix address space and develop an isometric hierarchical encoder-decoder that guarantees unique decodability. We further provide a practical Huffman-based procedure that embeds prefix-free, length-eigenstate codewords into the address space, thereby preserving isometry. The scheme is particularly designed for networks with hierarchical structure, heterogeneous cluster sizes, and configurable address assignment to accommodate dynamic network conditions. A numerical example on a 13-node network demonstrates that the proposed hierarchical encoding scheme is feasible and achieves perfect fidelity. This work establishes a rigorous connection between source coding theory and quantum network design, offering a practical framework towards scalable and coherent quantum addressing.
summary: This paper introduces a novel lossless source coding scheme designed to provide coherent and compact addressing within complex quantum networks. By structuring the address space hierarchically using prefix-suffix codes derived from local probability distributions, it ensures unique decodability without needing classical communication of node indices. This offers a practical framework for building scalable quantum infrastructure.
main_problem: The work addresses the critical need for a lossless source coding scheme to manage node identification and resource management in complex, interconnected quantum networks.
main_result: A hierarchical encoder-decoder structure is proposed that guarantees unique decodability while embedding necessary subspace information directly into the address state without requiring classical side channels.
method: The authors model addressing as an information-theoretic lossless source coding problem, utilizing a prefix-suffix address space and constructing isometric operators based on Huffman-like procedures derived from local source matrix diagonalization.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum network modeled as a graph partitioned into functional layers (Tier-2 ESP and Tier-1 User Nodes) and multiple clusters. The addressing function maps nodes to structured quantum address states $|\kappa_j\sigma_{ij}angle$.
key_observables: Perfect fidelity ($F(v)=1$) in the encoding/decoding process, isometry error ($\epsilon_{iso}$), and the structure of the resulting codeword state.
important_parameters: Cluster sizes, node probabilities derived from source matrices ($ho_e, ho_j$), and the maximum address length $\ell_{\max}$.
main_assumptions: The scheme assumes an ideal, noise-free environment for its primary demonstration; it also relies on the ability to construct isometries based on local probability distributions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the simple hierarchical quantum network model showing partitioning. Figure 2 (mentioned) illustrates the hierarchical decomposition of the source space $V$ into mutually orthogonal address subspaces $bA_j$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by defining the need for coherent addressing, then develops the mathematical framework using prefix-suffix coding and isometric operators derived from local source matrix diagonalization (Huffman procedure), culminating in proofs of unique decodability.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical link between classical information theory (source coding) and quantum network architecture design, offering concrete methods for scalable quantum resource management.
